target.title: feat(scheduler): prioritize exact-review backlog
target.body:
## Summary

- Prioritize only **healthy, target-admissible** exact-review backlog when choosing background review capacity.
- Preserve existing exact-review admission, leases, quotas, and the global worker budget; this change only reduces competing background work while the exact lane is demonstrably saturated.
- Publish `ready_pending` and `admissible_pending` queue telemetry, and log the selected background cap or an explicit fail-open warning in both review schedulers.

## Problem

The dashboard's global fleet capacity and the independently admitted exact-review lane are different resources. A saturated exact-review lane can have accepted work waiting even while the fleet has spare Codex budget. Background issue/PR and commit-review scheduling should yield some capacity in that specific, healthy condition rather than continue competing at its normal rate.

The current base also raises exact-review capacity and completes a lease before state-ledger publication. This PR is complementary: it does not change those queue mechanics, and it does not treat a public snapshot as permission to change admission.

## Implementation

- `dashboard/worker.ts` reports both:
  - `ready_pending`: pending items whose retry time is due;
  - `admissible_pending`: due items that can consume the next global exact-review slot after applying the same target-cap admission rule as the queue.
- `sweep.yml` and `commit-review.yml` classify pressure only when all of these are true:
  - exact lane is full (`dispatching + leased >= capacity`);
  - dispatcher is `active`;
  - handoff health is `healthy`;
  - `admissible_pending > 0`.
- A healthy full lane is `congested` when its admissible backlog is below lane capacity and `saturated` when it meets/exceeds that capacity. The configured background caps are 16 under congestion and 4 under saturation; the existing commit-review default of 6 stays below the congestion cap.
- Missing, malformed, or not-yet-deployed telemetry, retry-delayed work, target-cap-blocked work, paused dispatch, and degraded/stalled handoff all fail open to the normal scheduler behavior. The workflows emit a GitHub Actions warning when queue telemetry cannot be read.

## Validation

Ran from this branch after rebase onto `origin/main` (`3ab249b8c043366ace28f24779e4f2a4e7017853`):

```text
pnpm run build:all
node --test test/repair/workflow-utils.test.ts                         # 48 passed
node --test --test-name-pattern "background review schedulers yield" test/sweep-workflow.test.ts
node --test --test-name-pattern "dashboard status" test/dashboard-worker.test.ts  # 4 passed
pnpm lint repair
pnpm lint scripts
pnpm check:limits
pnpm exec oxfmt --check <the 10 touched files>
git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
```

- The full `test/sweep-workflow.test.ts` suite cannot run on this Windows host because its WSL Bash test helper lacks `/bin/bash`; the focused static scheduler test above passes.
- Docker actionlint was run against the repository. It reports pre-existing warnings/errors outside this PR's changed blocks: `exact-review-reconcile.yml:27`; `sweep.yml:240,527,824,2247,3516`. The last two are legacy `concurrency.queue` schema findings. No actionlint finding points to the changed scheduler blocks.

## Live and decision-table proof

At `2026-07-14T01:06:42Z`, the public status endpoint returned:

```text
generated_at=2026-07-14T01:05:56.953Z
pending=42; dispatching=11; leased=37
dispatcher=active; handoff=stalled
ready_pending=<not present>; admissible_pending=<not present>
```

That is expected before this dashboard change is deployed. Passing the missing `admissible_pending` value and stalled handoff into the compiled scheduler returns `idle`, proving the safe fail-open path; it does not throttle background review from an incomplete or unhealthy public snapshot.

The compiled local decision table returns:

```text
healthy full fixture with 48 admissible pending -> saturated
saturated normal_review cap                   -> 4
saturated hot_intake cap                      -> 4
saturated commit_review cap                   -> 4
stalled or missing-schema fixture             -> idle (fail open)
```

No direct workflow dispatch was used for this proof.

## Codex review closeout

- `codex review --uncommitted` was run during the fix loop; accepted findings were addressed by making pressure depend on queue admission rather than total pending work.
- Final `codex review --base origin/main` on the rebased head completed clean: **"No actionable correctness issues were identified in the changes relative to the specified merge base."**

## Risks and rollout

This is intentionally conservative: it can reduce background review throughput only while a healthy exact-review lane has backlog that is eligible for the next exact slot. It has no token, permission, queue-admission, lease, or state-publication change. Before the dashboard deployment reaches production, missing new telemetry leaves scheduler behavior unchanged.

target.title: fix(clickclack): redact REST error details
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ClickClack REST failures could include credential-shaped upstream or proxy response text in thrown errors when a non-2xx response body contained values such as bearer tokens or `access_token` parameters.

## Why This Change Was Made

The ClickClack client already bounds non-2xx response bodies before surfacing them. This change keeps that 8 KiB bound and the HTTP status detail, but runs the bounded text through the existing tool-payload redactor before constructing the error. That redaction path forces tool-mode masking even when operator log redaction is disabled, and it preserves built-in patterns when custom log patterns are configured. The fix stays at the ClickClack REST owner boundary and does not change request behavior, response parsing, retries, correlation IDs, or websocket handling.

## User Impact

Operators and users still get actionable ClickClack HTTP status and safe upstream diagnostic text, while obvious secret-shaped response content is masked before it can appear in logs or UI-visible failure messages.

## Evidence

### Regression Test

Added test `"redacts non-2xx response details independently of log redaction config"` in `extensions/clickclack/src/http-client.test.ts`. It verifies a mocked 502 response keeps safe diagnostic text while masking credential-shaped JSON fields when:

- `logging.redactSensitive` is disabled.
- custom `logging.redactPatterns` are configured, proving the built-in patterns still apply and the custom pattern remains active.

### Checks

```text
git diff --check -- extensions/clickclack/src/http-client.ts extensions/clickclack/src/http-client.test.ts
```

Passed.

```text
node --import tsx -e "<redaction helper probe with generated credential-shaped JSON fields>"
```

Passed. Confirmed both `logging.redactSensitive=off` and custom-pattern logging config produce masked credential field values while preserving the safe diagnostic field.

```text
python .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode commit --commit 785ef564fa1cc56237e1b8fef476967872276649
```

Passed: `autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported`.

### Current proof gap

Focused local Vitest could not complete in this checkout because the local dependency links are incomplete (`vitest` missing `pathe`). `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --force` both reported the workspace was already up to date and did not repair those links. This remains draft until CI/Testbox provides the focused test proof.

target.title: fix(gateway): don't retire parent Codex binding when creating a detached dashboard child
target.body:
Fixes #106778

## What Problem This Solves

Creating a dashboard child from an active Codex-backed channel session (Control UI → new dashboard chat — an ordinary child creation, not a fork) succeeds but **retires the parent session's Codex binding**, even though the parent remains the channel's current session. The next inbound parent turn then fails permanently with `Codex binding generation was retired`, recoverable only by manual SQLite surgery.

Root-cause chain (all on current `main`):
1. `createGatewaySession` emits a terminal `session_end(reason:"new")` on the **parent** for any parent-linked child when `emitCommandHooks === true` — `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts`.
2. The Codex extension treats `"new"` as terminal (`ENDED_SESSION_REASONS`) and its `session_end` handler calls `bindingStore.retireSessionGeneration()` — `extensions/codex/index.ts:48,274`.
3. The next lease attempt observes the retired generation and throws `Codex binding generation was retired`.

A detached dashboard child (its own `agent:<id>:dashboard:*` key) runs **in parallel** — it does not replace the parent as the channel's current session, so emitting a terminal `session_end` on the parent is wrong.

## Approach

The parent/child rollover pairs a terminal `session_end(parent)` with a `session_start(child)` — but that pairing is only correct when the child actually **succeeds** the parent. A detached dashboard child and a fork run in *parallel*: the parent stays current. So the two events are split — only the parent `session_end` is gated; the child's `session_start` always fires, because the child was in fact created:

```ts
const childSucceedsParent =
  params.fork !== true &&
  parseAgentSessionKey(target.canonicalKey)?.rest.startsWith("dashboard:") !== true;

if (canonicalParentSessionKey && parentSessionTarget && params.emitCommandHooks === true) {
  if (childSucceedsParent) {
    emitGatewaySessionEndPluginHook({ /* parent, reason:"new" */ });
  }
  emitGatewaySessionStartPluginHook({ /* child */ });
}
```

- **Detached dashboard child** / **fork** → no terminal `session_end` on the parent (the #106778 fix; also stops an accepted fork from retiring the parent binding), but the child still receives its `session_start`.
- **Legitimate rollover unchanged**: explicit `/new` successors use non-dashboard keys (`tui-*`) and still emit both; main reset-in-place emits its own hooks via `performGatewaySessionReset` and returns earlier.
- The parent's `before_reset` / `command:new` hooks (documented Control UI behavior, #76957) are untouched.

Fixing this in the gateway (where the parent is known to remain current) is the right layer; suppressing `"new"` in the Codex extension would also break legitimate TUI `/new` and reset-in-place retirement.

**Changed since first review (addresses the ClawSweeper P1):** the first revision suppressed the whole paired block for dashboard/fork, dropping the child's legitimate `session_start` alongside the parent's incorrect `session_end`. This revision decouples them — only the parent `session_end` is gated, the child `session_start` is preserved (the Control UI contract from #78215) — and adds fork + `emitCommandHooks` regression coverage.

Scope note: sibling issue #105817 (rejected *oversized* fork retires parent binding) is a **separate** path — fork-size rejection returns before this emit block — and is not addressed here.

## Evidence

**A/B against real service code** (Node 25.9.0 + SQLite 3.51.3, Linux). Same detached-dashboard-child test, toggling only the parent-`session_end` gate. The gateway session-create path itself runs for real; the downstream plugin hooks are the observation point (`vi.fn`):

```
B) WITHOUT the gate (force parent session_end):
   FAIL — AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" [runSessionEnd] to not be called
   at all, but actually been called 1 times
   -> the parent receives session_end for a detached dashboard child (the bug)

A) WITH the fix:
   Tests  1 passed
   -> no parent session_end; child session_start still emitted
```

The consequence side is mechanically traceable in-repo: `session_end(reason:"new")` → `ENDED_SESSION_REASONS` (`extensions/codex/index.ts:48`) → `retireSessionGeneration` (`:274`) → the exact `{"state":"cleared","retired":true}` binding row #106778 reports.

- **Focused suites** (`server.sessions.reset-hooks.test.ts` + `server.sessions.create.test.ts`): **62 passed** — the dashboard child asserts *no* parent `session_end` but *does* assert a child `session_start` (resumedFrom parent, dashboard-keyed); a **new** fork + `emitCommandHooks` test asserts the same; legitimate rollover (`/new` `tui-*`, reset-in-place) still asserts both hooks.
- **Preservation** — `extensions/codex/` (2500 tests / 106 files) passed: a genuine `session_end reason:"new"` still retires the binding, so the fix does not weaken legitimate retirement.
- **Static**: `tsgo` clean on changed files; `oxlint` clean.

A full Codex app-server E2E (real binding row before/after a live dashboard-child creation) would exercise only the same gateway dispatch these tests drive directly, plus the extension handler already covered by the preservation suite — happy to add one if a maintainer prefers that shape.

## Tests

`server.sessions.reset-hooks.test.ts` (detached dashboard child → `before_reset`/`command:new` yes, terminal parent `session_end` no, child `session_start` yes; reset-in-place + `/new` `tui-*` → still both), `server.sessions.create.test.ts` (selected-global dashboard child → no parent `session_end`, child `session_start`; **new** fork + `emitCommandHooks` → no parent `session_end`, child `session_start`), `extensions/codex/` (genuine `session_end` still retires — preservation).

target.title: fix(agents): classify Anthropic invalid_request_error as format for failover
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: Anthropic-style HTTP 400 error responses arrive as raw JSON bodies with no leading HTTP status prefix. The failover classifier cannot infer the HTTP status via `extractLeadingHttpStatus` and returns `null`, so the configured model fallback chain is never consulted — users see a terminal error despite healthy fallback models being available.

**Solution**: Added a check in `classifyFailoverClassificationFromMessage` that detects `invalid_request_error` from the structured API error type via the existing `parseApiErrorInfo` helper and classifies it as `"format"`, which triggers the model fallback chain. The check is placed after auth/billing/rate-limit/context-overflow classifiers so more specific reasons take precedence. `isModelNotFoundErrorMessage` is checked before `isStructuredInvalidRequestError` to ensure model-unavailable semantics are preserved when the payload indicates a model-not-found condition (#101414 review fix).

Also fixed `isSchemaErrorMessage()` to exclude structured `invalid_request_error` payloads. Without this exclusion, `isSchemaErrorMessage` would match via `classifyFailoverReason(raw) === "format"` and `classifyProviderRuntimeFailureKind` would incorrectly return `"schema"` instead of `"format"`, defeating the primary fix's effect in the runtime-failure path.

**What changed**: 7 files, ~+182/-4 lines — one classifier rule addition in `errors.ts` (line 1146), reordered `isModelNotFoundErrorMessage` before `isStructuredInvalidRequestError` to preserve model_not_found precedence (review fix #101414), one early-exit guard in `isSchemaErrorMessage()` (line 599) to prevent schema/format collision, one whitelist entry in `result-fallback-classifier.ts` (belt-and-suspenders), a `runWithModelFallback` integration test in `model-fallback.test.ts` to exercise the actual fallback machinery, a `result-fallback-classifier.test.ts` regression, a `failover-error.test.ts` cover, and a formatter-sync test in `formatassistanterrortext.test.ts`. Total: 14 new test cases across 5 test files (+1 updated for model_not_found precedence).

**What NOT changed**: No provider connections, no credentials, no configuration schema, no public API signatures, no lockfile or changelog.

Fixes #99174

---

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: classifyFailoverReason returns "format" (instead of null) for Anthropic invalid_request_error JSON bodies.
**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v25.9.0, OpenClaw main @ ae397906aa
**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `npx tsx docs/.local/issue-99174-evidence.ts` against actual exported classifiers with realistic Anthropic error payloads
**After-fix evidence**: classifyFailoverReason returns "format" for invalid_request_error (with and without HTTP 400 prefix), and returns "model_not_found" when the payload contains model-not-found semantics (isModelNotFoundErrorMessage takes precedence). Result-level classifier returns {reason: "format"} for non-model payloads. `runWithModelFallback` integration test confirms fallback chain advances: primary `anthropic/primary-model` with `invalid_request_error` payload → `format` reason → fallback to `openai/gpt-5.5` succeeds. Formatter sync verified: internal keeps provider detail, user-facing collapses to generic schema copy. **5 test files, 361 tests — all passed.**
**Observed result after the fix**: classifyFailoverReason returns "format" for invalid_request_error bodies, correctly triggering the FailoverError machinery and advancing the model fallback chain in the integrated `runWithModelFallback` path.
**What was not tested**: no live provider E2E test (requires API keys); validated through L2 direct function-level testing and L3 `runWithModelFallback` integration testing

### Terminal transcript — L2 evidence run

Input payload (realistic Anthropic invalid_request_error):
```
{"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"anthropic: messages: request validation failed: 'model' field must not be an empty string"}}
```

Output:
```
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  L2 Evidence: Anthropic invalid_request_error → 'format' fallback
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

── Test 1: classifyFailoverReason ──────────────────────────────
  ✅ invalid_request_error (no prefix) → 'format': got: format
  ✅ invalid_request_error (with 400 prefix) → 'format': got: format
  ✅ authentication_error → NOT 'format': got: auth
  ✅ plain text error → NOT 'format': got: null

── Test 2: isFailoverErrorMessage ─────────────────────────────
  ✅ invalid_request_error → isFailoverErrorMessage: true
  ✅ authentication_error → isFailoverErrorMessage: true

── Test 3: result-level classifier ─────────────────────────────
  ✅ classifyEmbeddedAgentRunResultForModelFallback returns {reason: "format"}

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  Result: ✅ ALL PASSED (7/7)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
```

## Root Cause

5 Whys traced the issue to `classifyFailoverClassificationFromMessage` in `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts` (line 1029). The function extracts HTTP status via `extractLeadingHttpStatus` but Anthropic JSON bodies have no leading prefix. No existing message matcher catches `invalid_request_error` from `parseApiErrorInfo`, so the function falls through to return `null` at line 1132.

### Review fix (#101414)

During review, ClawSweeper identified that `isStructuredInvalidRequestError` was checked before `isModelNotFoundErrorMessage`, causing structured `invalid_request_error` payloads with model-not-found semantics (e.g. `"model not found for inference"`) to be demoted from `"model_not_found"` to `"format"`, losing existing model-unavailable warning behavior.

**Fix**: Reordered the checks in `classifyFailoverClassificationFromMessage` — `isModelNotFoundErrorMessage` now runs before `isStructuredInvalidRequestError`. This ensures that when an `invalid_request_error` body also matches model-not-found patterns, the more specific `model_not_found` classification takes precedence. Non-model `invalid_request_error` payloads (thinking-block edits, request validation errors) still correctly classify as `"format"`.

## Linked context

- **Issue**: #99174
- **Related**: #92201 (thinking-signature root cause), #99184 (competing PR)
- **In scope**: Failover classification of `invalid_request_error` JSON bodies
- **Out of scope**: Fixing the provider-side root cause that produces these errors

All tests pass with zero regressions:

```
 ✓  40 passed (failover-matches.test.ts)
 ✓  21 passed (result-fallback-classifier.test.ts)
 ✓  90 passed (formatassistanterrortext.test.ts)
 ✓  94 passed (failover-error.test.ts)
 ✓ 116 passed (model-fallback.test.ts)
 ─────────────────────
 ✓ 361 total — all passed
```

### Integration test: runWithModelFallback

New test `"continues fallback after embedded structured invalid_request_error payloads (#99174)"`:
- Config: `anthropic/primary-model → fallbacks: [openai/gpt-5.5]`
- Primary run returns `invalid_request_error` JSON body (no HTTP prefix) as error payload
- `classifyEmbeddedAgentRunResultForModelFallback` returns `{ reason: "format" }`
- `runWithModelFallback` advances to fallback `openai/gpt-5.5`
- Final result: `{ text: "fallback ok" }`
- Assertions: `run` called 2 times, fallback model used, `format` reason recorded in attempts

### Formatter sync test

New test `"keeps internal detail and user-facing redaction in sync for #99174 fallback bodies"`:
- `formatAssistantErrorText` (internal) keeps provider detail: contains "messages.27.content.1"
- `formatUserFacingAssistantErrorText` (user-facing) returns: "LLM request failed: provider rejected the request schema or tool payload."

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary

- Auth-provider risk: Low — only classification logic changed, no provider connections touched.
- Merge-risk: 🚨 other — narrow classification addition; verified by 35 existing + 4 new tests.

- [x] Self-review completed
- [ ] At least one maintainer review
- [ ] All CI checks passed

target.title: fix(signal): bound container receive websocket handshake waits at 30s
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal container receive streaming created the long-lived `/v1/receive` WebSocket with `maxPayload` but no `handshakeTimeout`. `streamContainerEvents` waits for the connection lifecycle (`open` / `close`); when a peer accepts TCP but never completes the websocket upgrade, that wait never ends, so `runSignalSseLoop` cannot reconnect. The probe path in the same file already times out; only the long-lived receive path was missing a hang floor. Slack relay and Mattermost already bound handshake waits at 30s.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Keep a private `buildSignalContainerWebSocketOptions` as the single production options surface (`maxPayload` + `handshakeTimeout: 30_000`).
- Probe and long-lived receive both consume that builder.
- Regressions observe production wiring in source (knip-safe; no new unused exports) and prove stalled-handshake timeout returns control from `streamContainerEvents`.

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** A Signal container that accepted TCP without completing the websocket handshake could pin the receive reconnect loop forever on that attempt.

**After:** Handshake waits fail closed after 30s (`Opening handshake has timed out` / close), allowing `runSignalSseLoop` to continue reconnecting.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/signal/src/client-container.ts`
- Production caller: `streamContainerEvents` → `streamSignalEvents` → `runSignalSseLoop`
- Sibling: `extensions/slack/src/monitor/relay-source.ts` (`handshakeTimeout: 30_000`); Mattermost `#105553`
- Asymmetry proof: same-file probe already timed out; long-lived receive did not
- Regression: `extensions/signal/src/client-container.test.ts`, `extensions/signal/src/client-container.ws-handshake.test.ts`

### Caller-path Vitest

target.title: fix(codex): stop warning when a non-Codex-native run has no mirrored history
target.body:
> Resubmit of #106912, which was auto-closed by the active-PR-limit bot. Same tested commit; unchanged.

## What Problem This Solves

The Codex app-server harness also runs non-OpenAI models (Claude/Haiku). On those runs — and on the first turn of any new session — there is no Codex-native mirrored session transcript to read, which is expected. `readMirroredSessionHistoryMessages()` nonetheless emitted a `warn` ("failed to read mirrored session history for codex harness hooks") on every such turn, and channels render that `agent/embedded` warn as `⚠️ 🧰 Process: <name> failed`, so operators see a routine, non-fatal condition as an error. (Reported in #106556.)

## Why This Change Was Made

`readCodexMirroredSessionHistoryMessages()` already distinguishes the cases: a missing file (ENOENT) returns `[]`, and a present-but-not-Codex-native mirror returns `undefined`. Every caller tolerates the miss and falls back to existing history (`?? []`, `?? historyState.messages`), so the `undefined` return is expected control flow, not a failure. The wrapper's warning also carried no error cause (only `sessionFile`), so it was low signal. This change downgrades it from `warn` to `debug` with clearer wording — the minimal, behavior-preserving fix (no control-flow or return-contract change) for a path under the Codex extension gate. The `undefined` return stays load-bearing for the two call sites that fall back to prior history.

Note: this is a log-severity change on OpenClaw's own mirrored-session reader (OpenClaw session-entry format), not Codex wire-protocol or runtime behavior.

## User Impact

Non-Codex-native and first-turn runs routed through the Codex harness no longer surface a spurious failed "Process" to operators. Genuine failures were already swallowed upstream and are unaffected; the run still completes via the existing fallback.

## Evidence

- New regression in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.test.ts`: a mirror whose first entry is not a `session` header returns `undefined`, emits **no** `warn`, and logs `debug` instead. Full file green (6 passed) via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.test.ts`. The prior "missing history → [] without warn" test still passes.
- `git diff --check` clean; 2 files, +35/−1; no `CHANGELOG.md` edit.
- Source-reproducible: the noise is a fixed `warn` on an expected `undefined` return; a live Codex run is not needed to demonstrate it.

Fixes #106556

target.title: fix(tlon): clear SSE connect timeout after failed openStream
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Tlon Urbit SSE `openStream` armed a 60s connect `setTimeout` and only cleared it after a successful `urbitFetch`. When the connect fetch rejected (DNS/SSRF/network) or returned non-OK, the timer stayed armed until it fired, and reconnect storms could stack dangling timers in the Gateway process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wrap the connect fetch in `try/finally` and always `clearTimeout`, matching the zalouser probe timeout cleanup pattern, so failed connects release the timer immediately without changing the connect deadline or stream lifecycle.

## User Impact

Flaky Urbit hosts no longer leave dangling connect timers in long-running Tlon monitors during reconnect failures.

## Evidence

### Unit regression (mocked fetch + fake timers)

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/tlon/src/urbit/sse-client.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

```text
 ✓ ... > openStream > clears the connect timeout when urbitFetch rejects 12ms
 ✓ ... > openStream > clears the connect timeout when the stream response is not ok 10ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  18 passed (18)
```

### Production-path connect-timeout storm proof

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/tlon/src/urbit/sse-client.open-stream-timeout.proof.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

```text
 ✓ ... > clears connect timers after a real non-OK stream response storm 305ms
 ✓ ... > clears the connect timer when production urbitFetch rejects 10ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

The storm case runs production `openStream` → `urbitFetch` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` against a real loopback `node:http` server that returns `503` five times; real timers; each armed `setTimeout(..., 60000)` is cleared. The reject case uses a closed loopback port (`127.0.0.1:9`) so the production transport fails before headers.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Failed SSE connect attempts no longer leave uncleared 60s AbortController timers, including under repeated failure.
- **Canonical reachability path:** Tlon monitor reconnect → `UrbitSSEClient.openStream` → production `urbitFetch` / `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → reject or non-OK → `finally { clearTimeout(timeoutId) }`.
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime HTTP; loopback `node:http` + closed-port TCP failure; production SSRF-guarded transport (no `urbitFetch` mock, no fake timers).
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Same `try/finally { clearTimeout }` pattern as `extensions/zalouser/src/probe.ts`; no new config/API.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, Node via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` with real HTTP listeners and real timers.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/tlon/src/urbit/sse-client.open-stream-timeout.proof.test.ts extensions/tlon/src/urbit/sse-client.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
 ✓ |extension-messaging| ... > clears the connect timeout when urbitFetch rejects 12ms
 ✓ |extension-messaging| ... > clears the connect timeout when the stream response is not ok 10ms
 ✓ |extension-messaging| ... > clears connect timers after a real non-OK stream response storm 305ms
 ✓ |extension-messaging| ... > clears the connect timer when production urbitFetch rejects 10ms
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  20 passed (20)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 7.90s
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Five sequential non-OK connects each arm then clear a 60s connect timer with matching `clearTimeout(handle)`; a real transport reject also clears its single connect timer.
- **What was not tested:** Live Urbit ship reconnect storm against a real Tlon host; SSE stream body processing after a successful connect.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

## Risk / Compatibility

Low. Successful connects still clear the timer after headers; only failed connects gain the missing cleanup.

target.title: fix(memory): hide QMD transport metadata from recalled content
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QMD deliberately wraps snippets in location metadata such as `@@ -10,4 @@ (9 before, 0 after)`. Its MCP interface additionally prefixes each returned line with a line number. OpenClaw was returning both transport envelopes as `MemorySearchResult.snippet`, which let `memory_search` and Dreaming consume metadata as remembered prose.

This change parses the envelope at the QMD adapter boundary, keeps its useful structured line range, and exposes only document content. It also normalizes already-persisted short-term recall entries and regenerates their concept tags.

Closes #106937
Related: #89444, #71030

## Why

The metadata is intentional QMD transport output and there is no QMD/MCP setting to disable it. Fixing the adapter is preferable to patching QMD, adding a proxy service, or weakening retrieval quality.

The parser is deliberately conservative:

- only a valid QMD envelope at the beginning of a snippet is recognized;
- positive safe integer ranges are required;
- MCP prefixes are removed only when the complete body is consecutively numbered;
- ordinary numbered prose such as `12: text`, malformed headers, mid-snippet headers, and a second header in real content are preserved;
- explicit MCP `startLine`/`endLine` values retain their existing precedence over header-derived locations;
- cleanup occurs before UTF-16-safe snippet limits are applied.

## User Impact

- `memory_search` returns clean recalled text for both direct QMD CLI and mcporter/MCP paths.
- Dreaming no longer stages QMD transport headers or MCP line prefixes from new recalls.
- The existing short-term repair command cleans stored envelopes, remains idempotent, and recalculates derived concept tags.
- Search mode, reranking, scoring, collection routing, and persistent mcporter behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Before

```text
11: @@ -10,4 @@ (9 before, 0 after)
12: first remembered line
13:
14: 12: legitimate numbered prose
```

### After

```text
first remembered line

12: legitimate numbered prose
```

Structured location remains `startLine: 10`, `endLine: 13`.

### Validation

Validated after rebasing onto current `origin/main` with safe Node 24.18.0:

- `qmd-snippet.test.ts`: 13/13 passed.
- `short-term-promotion.test.ts`: 72/72 passed.
- Focused QMD integration selection: 11/11 passed, including both single-endpoint line-range branches.
- Strict standalone TypeScript check for the new parser: passed.
- Changed files: `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent post-implementation review: approved with no unaddressed findings.

A full extensions type-check on current main also reports unrelated dependency/type failures outside this patch. It initially caught strict capture-index errors in the new parser; those were fixed, and the parser now passes an isolated strict TypeScript check.

The repository autoreview launcher could not invoke a shell review engine in this OpenClaw-native Codex environment, so an independent native Codex review was run against the actual diff instead.

Remote Crabbox validation was attempted but unavailable in this environment: the configured Blacksmith provider has no `blacksmith` executable, and the AWS fallback has no usable credentials. No untrusted patch was run outside the repository checkout.

## AI Assistance

This patch was implemented with Codex assistance. The behavior was independently audited before and after implementation, and all reported findings were verified against source and tests.

Maintainers may edit this branch.

## What Problem This Solves

Reef inbox monitoring uses the WHATWG `WebSocket` (not the `ws` package), so there is no `handshakeTimeout` option. `ReefInboxConnection.live()` only settles on `close` / `error` / channel `abort`. When a peer accepts TCP but never completes the websocket upgrade, `start()` waits forever on `await live()` and the reconnect backoff loop never advances.

## User Impact

target.title: fix(auto-reply): self-heal reply-session-init conflict instead of permanently wedging the session
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Fixes #101909.

The reply-session initializer's conflict branch in `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts` allowed a single stale-snapshot retry and then threw `reply session initialization conflicted for <sessionKey>`. Because initialization never completed, the session-store entry was never committed and the session wedged **permanently** for that `sessionKey`: every subsequent turn re-hit the same conflict, completed tool executions (`exec`/`read`/etc.) had no channel back to the model, and tool-results silently returned empty. It survived gateway restarts (the conflict is keyed to the persistent sessionKey) and cleared only on a fresh session or `/reset`.

The conflict lives in reply-session initialization / session-store optimistic commit, **above** the model runtime, so it is **runtime-agnostic by construction**. Every case we observed live ran under the Codex app-server harness; on that harness the never-written transcript mirror (`<session>.jsonl.codex-app-server.json`, which carries the threadId) is a runtime-specific casualty, but the root cause is the conflict branch failing to recover — not anything Codex-specific.

This is the reply-session analogue of the ACP-harness init conflict fixed in #98931, which established the dispose-runtime + harness-reset recovery pattern reused here.

## Fix
The rollover/timeout paths already self-heal by disposing the session's MCP runtime and running the registered harness `reset` hooks. This change makes the conflict branch reuse that same recovery **once** and retry initialization before giving up:

1. stale-snapshot retry (unchanged — benign concurrent-revision case)
2. if still conflicted: dispose the wedged runtime + run harness self-heal, then retry init exactly once (recursion bounded by `conflictRecoveryAttempted`)
3. if it still cannot commit: throw with clear context instead of leaving the session able to silently return empty tool-results

**Safety fence (commit `ede72284b`):** the first version of the self-heal called the teardown primitives inline while holding `runExclusiveSessionStoreWrite`. That lock does not block a foreign turn's execution, so a genuinely active concurrent turn on the same sessionKey (hot topic / rapid messages / rollover racing a fresh turn) could be disposed mid-flight, and draining inside the lock could deadlock. The self-heal now routes through the same fence the rollover path uses: it drains foreign work admissions via `interruptSessionWorkAdmissions` **outside** the store-write lock before disposing the wedged runtime and retrying. No new machinery — it reuses `runExclusiveSessionLifecycleMutation` + `interruptSessionWorkAdmissions`.

The decision logic is isolated in a small pure helper (`src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.ts`) with unit tests.

## Evidence
**Focused tests**
- `npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts` → **142/142 pass** (4 decider unit tests + 138 session tests, including 2 new integration tests driving the real `session.ts` wiring: a forced double commit conflict disposes the wedged MCP runtime and completes in exactly 3 commit attempts; an actively-admitted foreign turn is interrupted/drained before teardown rather than torn down).
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` → no type errors in changed files (only pre-existing, unrelated errors in `src/plugins/providers.test.ts`).

**Live proof.** Captured on a real OpenClaw 2026.6.11 host. The wedge reproduced on **two independent agents / sessionKeys**, each re-hitting the identical conflict on the same persistent sessionKey for the same inbound message across repeated retries — a permanent wedge, not a transient race. Group/topic identifiers redacted; structure and error text preserved.

```
# Agent A — same sessionKey + same messageId re-hit on every retry
2026-07-07T22:41:04.633Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<A>:telegram:group:<redacted>:topic:<redacted> messageId=<M1> outcome=error error="Error: reply session initialization conflicted for agent:<A>:telegram:group:<redacted>:topic:<redacted>"
2026-07-07T22:41:10.189Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<A>...:topic:<redacted> messageId=<M1> outcome=error error="Error: reply session initialization conflicted ..."
2026-07-07T22:41:20.687Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<A>...:topic:<redacted> messageId=<M1> outcome=error
2026-07-07T22:41:41.222Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<A>...:topic:<redacted> messageId=<M1> outcome=error
2026-07-07T22:42:21.772Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<A>...:topic:<redacted> messageId=<M1> outcome=error

# Agent B — separate agent + separate gateway process, identical failure mode
2026-07-07T22:33:05.485Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<B>:telegram:group:<redacted> messageId=<M2> outcome=error error="Error: reply session initialization conflicted for agent:<B>:telegram:group:<redacted>"
2026-07-07T22:33:10.578Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<B>:telegram:group:<redacted> messageId=<M2> outcome=error
2026-07-07T22:34:21.172Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<B>:telegram:group:<redacted> messageId=<M2> outcome=error
```

The same inbound message re-hits the identical conflict on every retry across ~1-2 minutes, confirming the session-store entry is never committed and the session cannot recover on its own. Operational mitigation before this fix was `/reset` or a fresh session.

**After-fix live proof (patched build, live end-to-end gateway; plus stock 2026.6.11 A/B).** Captured 2026-07-08 on a scratch, isolated gateway (disposable VM, loopback-only bind, token auth, live Anthropic model) driving the real WebChat reply path via the documented gateway-client WS handshake and `chat.send`. Identical harness and trigger on both builds. Session identifiers are synthetic (`pr101920-live`); hosts/IPs/paths redacted.

*Trigger (real code path, no mocks):* seed `sessions.json` with a wedge-shaped entry so reply-session init adopts sessionId `pr101920-live-wedged`; start a long-running **hold** exec turn as a real in-flight admission of that identity; an external **toucher** process continuously rewrites the entry's `sessionFile` (atomic tmp+rename) so the **probe** turn's init snapshot→commit revision guard keeps losing the optimistic-concurrency race; the toucher stops once the self-heal marker appears so the post-heal retry can commit. Calibration honesty: fixed-cadence bumps (8ms, then 1ms) produced **0** conflicts — the snapshot→commit window is sub-millisecond; only continuous spin-writes reproduce the repeated-conflict wedge live. Non-triggering calibration runs are preserved alongside the golden artifacts.

*Patched build (PR head `09aac6a`) — self-heal fires, fenced drain works, turn completes with real tool output:*

```

2026-07-08T23:30:53.787+00:00 [session-init] reply session initialization conflicted for agent:main:webchat:direct:pr101920-live; requesting fenced harness self-heal before final retry
2026-07-08T23:30:53.798+00:00 [session-init] reply session initialization conflicted for agent:main:webchat:direct:pr101920-live; requesting fenced harness self-heal before final retry

message processed: channel=webchat chatId=unknown messageId=optionb-hold-20260708T233043Z sessionId=pr101920-live-wedged sessionKey=agent:main:webchat:direct:pr101920-live outcome=completed duration=9432ms reason=reply_operation_aborted
```

Probe turn final WS frame at 23:31:20.17 — `"state":"final","stopReason":"stop"`, and the healed session's reply body carries the actual `exec` output:

```
The exact tool output is:

PR101920_REAL_TOOL_OUTPUT_NONEMPTY
```

Whole patched run: **0 `outcome=error` events** and **0** `Error: reply session initialization conflicted` throws in the gateway log. The final committed session store (`sessions.final.json`) contains the previously-uncommittable entry for the wedged sessionKey — the healed init retry committed it (with the toucher's last `sessionFile` write), which is exactly what the pre-fix wedge could never do.

*Stock `openclaw@2026.6.11` (npm) — same trigger, user-visible hard failure:*

```
2026-07-08T23:35:59.292+00:00 [diagnostic] message dispatch completed: channel=webchat sessionId=unknown sessionKey=agent:main:webchat:direct:pr101920-live source=replyResolver outcome=error duration=17ms error="Error: reply session initialization conflicted for agent:main:webchat:direct:pr101920-live"
2026-07-08T23:35:59.296+00:00 [diagnostic] message processed: channel=webchat chatId=unknown messageId=optionb-probe-20260708T233503Z sessionId=pr101920-live-wedged sessionKey=agent:main:webchat:direct:pr101920-live outcome=error duration=51444ms error="Error: reply session initialization conflicted for agent:main:webchat:direct:pr101920-live"
```

WS client terminal frame — the assistant's final message body **is** the conflict error, and no assistant delta/final frame ever carried the tool output:

```
"state":"error","errorMessage":"Error: reply session initialization conflicted for agent:main:webchat:direct:pr101920-live","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Error: reply session initialization conflicted for agent:main:webchat:direct:pr101920-live"}]}
```

Stock contains no self-heal marker (0 occurrences) and the toucher ran to its timeout (no marker to stop on).

*Stored-state compatibility observed live:* both builds ran against identically seeded `sessions.json` files in the current 2026.6.11 shape; the patched build read and committed that store with no schema change — `sessions.final.json` is a standard sessions map (same fields, no new/renamed keys).

## Scope
This addresses the conflict-wedge failure mode. It does not attempt to address a separate operational failure where the Codex app-server child is not running at all — a different cause that presents the same empty-tool-result surface.

target.title: fix(sandbox): use canonical shortenHomePath for sandbox-root escape error
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The local `shortPath` helper in `src/agents/sandbox-paths.ts` shortened any path whose string prefix matched the home directory, with no path-separator boundary. A sandbox root that is a *sibling* of the home directory therefore rendered mangled in the "Path escapes sandbox root" error: with home `/Users/al` and root `/Users/albert/proj`, the message read `~bert/proj` instead of `/Users/albert/proj`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The other home-path shorteners in the tree already guard the boundary — `src/utils.ts` `shortenHomePath`, `src/agents/sessions/tools/render-utils.ts` `shortenPath`, `src/agents/sandbox/fs-paths.ts` `shortenHomePath`. This local `shortPath` was the last unguarded copy of the same idea. Rather than add a fourth boundary check, delete the duplicate and reuse the canonical `shortenHomePath` from `../utils`, matching the repo's "one canonical path, delete the duplicate" policy.

## User Impact

Cosmetic: the sandbox-root-escape error message now renders a home-sibling root correctly instead of a mangled `~…` path. No change for a root actually under the home directory (still `~/…`) or fully outside it (unchanged). No config, API, or storage surface is touched — the diff is one import plus the deletion of the six-line local helper.

## Evidence

Repro of the boundary difference (the removed `shortPath` logic vs the canonical `shortenHomePath` semantics):

```
/Users/albert/proj   shortPath -> ~bert/proj      shortenHomePath -> /Users/albert/proj
/Users/al/work       shortPath -> ~/work          shortenHomePath -> ~/work
/tmp/x               shortPath -> /tmp/x           shortenHomePath -> /tmp/x
```

`shortenHomePath` is the canonical boundary-safe helper (it checks `input === home` and `input.startsWith(home + separator)`) and is already covered by `src/utils.test.ts`. `os` stays imported because `expandPath` in the same file still uses `os.homedir()`.

Disclosure: I verified this statically (the repro above plus the existing `shortenHomePath` coverage); I did not run the remote Testbox/Crabbox suite from my fork checkout. The change is a straight dedupe onto an already-tested helper.

target.title: fix(security): add estimate-before-decode guard to base64 paths
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large base64-encoded images can cause transient memory pressure during decoding. This PR adds a size estimation check before decoding base64 image data in CLI staging and provider image-parsing paths, and propagates the existing configured media size limit through these new guards.

**Security impact**: Defense-in-depth against transient memory exhaustion from oversized base64 payloads.

## Summary

- Added `estimateBase64DecodedSize` helper that estimates decoded byte length from base64 input
- Propagated existing `maxBytes` limit through:
  - CLI image writing (`writeCliImages`)
  - Provider image parsing (`generatedImageAssetFromBase64`)
- Added boundary tests for:
  - Configured limit acceptance (7MB payload under 8MB limit)
  - Over-limit rejection before decoding
  - Default limit enforcement (6 MiB)
- **No new configuration**: Uses existing `generatedMediaMaxBytes` setting

## Evidence

**Environment**: macOS Vitest (Node 22.22.2)

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
# Run configured limit test
npx vitest run src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts
```

**Observed result after fix**:
```text
✓ agents-core src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts (30 tests) 203ms
✓ agents-support src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts (30 tests) 184ms

Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests  60 passed (60)

Key test coverage:
✓ rejects base64 image that exceeds size limit
✓ accepts images above MAX_IMAGE_BYTES when a higher configured maxBytes is provided
  - 7MB payload accepted under 8MB configured limit (line 322-346)
  - 10MB payload rejected under 8MB limit
  - 7MB payload rejected under default 6MiB limit (no maxBytes)
```

**Configuration limit propagation verified**:
- Test file: `src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts:322-346`
- Scenario: 7MB payload (above default 6MiB) accepted when 8MB limit configured
- Code path: `writeCliImages` receives `maxBytes: 8 * 1024 * 1024`, checks pass

**What was not tested**: Live provider OOM reproduction (neither necessary nor safely desirable)

## Regression Test Plan
- Coverage: 60 tests across 2 test suites
- Target files: `src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts`, `src/image-generation/image-assets.test.ts`
- Scenarios locked in:
  - Estimated size < maxBytes: accept
  - Estimated size > maxBytes: reject before decode
  - Configured limit > default: use configured
  - No configured limit: use default 6 MiB

target.title: fix(subagents): credit requester-consumed descendant completions
target.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a lifecycle/delivery accounting gap for background and cron-owned subagent trees: when a requester actually consumes completed descendant subagent output, the descendant run is now durably credited as delivered instead of later being finalized as failed/suspended solely because no separate visible delivery event occurred.

## What Problem This Solves

Requester-owned subagent trees can legitimately consume descendant output without sending a separate descendant-visible delivery event. This is common for cron/background flows where a parent/requester gathers frozen child output, composes its own result, and then delivers that requester result outward. Before this PR, the descendant completion could remain delivery-unproven even though its output had already been consumed by the requester. Later cleanup/finalization could then classify that descendant as failed or suspended, producing delivery state that did not match real behavior. This PR gives the registry an explicit durable signal for that case: requester consumption is delivery evidence only for the exact descendant runs that were consumed, under the matching requester session/run-start window, when the requester path adopts descendant fallback output, so the consumed descendant rows do not later announce or finalize as pending just because the final outward send fails.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

When OpenClaw can prove that a requester consumed descendant subagent output, the matching descendant run receives durable delivery credit:
- `delivery.status` is set to `"delivered"` for the matched descendant completion;
- requester-consumption metadata is persisted with the run/delivery state;
- cleanup/finalize treats `delivery.status === "delivered"` as completed delivery proof;
- normal visible-delivery paths remain required for completions that were not consumed by a requester.
The matching is intentionally narrow. Credit is only applied when all of these are true:
- the consumed run IDs are explicit;
- the requester session key matches;
- the requester run-start window matches the consuming requester run;
- the consumption kind is known;
- cron fallback credit happens when cron adopts explicit descendant fallback output for the requester result;
- nested subagent announcement credit only covers direct child run IDs that were actually included in the requester-consumed output.

This PR keeps the delivery model explicit:
- if a descendant result was visibly delivered, it is delivered;
- if a requester consumed the descendant output because cron adopted it as the requester result, the descendant is delivered by requester consumption;
- if neither happened, failure/suspension handling still applies.

## Linked Context

- Related issue: #92433 — subagent completion can be silently dropped when an announce handoff reaches a requester transcript but the requester run ends before consuming it. This PR addresses the adjacent durable-accounting problem for completions that *are* consumed by a requester.
- Related issue: #67777 — subagent completion delivery can be lost on direct-announce timeout, drain, or orphan prune. This PR does not implement the full durable inbox/spool requested there, but it narrows one delivery-accounting gap by recording proven requester consumption.
- Related issue: #86537 — suspended final delivery can expire and discard a pending subagent completion. This PR keeps requester-consumed completions from remaining indistinguishable from undelivered completions in finalization state.
- Related issue: #90299 — subagent lifecycle state can report lost active execution context while still surfacing child output. This PR contributes to lifecycle/state consistency when descendant output is actually consumed.
- Related PR: #92934 — required assistant acknowledgement for completion wake handoffs, so transcript commit alone is not treated as requester consumption. This PR complements that by adding durable credit for explicit consumed descendant run IDs.
- Related PR: #35080 — deterministic subagent announce delivery with descendant gating. This PR builds on that direction by making consumed descendant accounting durable.
- Related PR: #44205 — stale descendant cron fallback summaries. This PR keeps the same stale-vs-current discipline for requester-consumed descendant credit.
- Related PR: #95604 — Discord subagent progress feedback. This PR is not a Discord UI change, but accurate delivered/failed lifecycle state is useful to progress/failure-marker consumers.
No exact existing issue/PR was found for `markDescendantCompletionConsumedByRequester` or this exact requester-consumed credit mechanism, so this PR should stand as the focused implementation thread for that behavior.

## What Changes

When OpenClaw can prove that a requester consumed descendant subagent output, the matching descendant run receives durable delivery credit:
- `delivery.status` is set to `"delivered"` for the matched descendant completion;
- requester-consumption metadata is persisted with the run/delivery state;
- cleanup/finalize treats `delivery.status === "delivered"` as completed delivery proof;
- normal visible-delivery paths remain required for completions that were not consumed by a requester.
The matching is intentionally narrow. Credit is only applied when all of these are true:
- the consumed run IDs are explicit;
- the requester session key matches;
- the requester run-start window matches the consuming requester run;
- the consumption kind is known;
- cron fallback credit happens when cron adopts explicit descendant fallback output for the requester result;
- nested subagent announcement credit only covers direct child run IDs that were actually included in the requester-consumed output.

## Implementation Notes

Core registry/runtime changes:
- Adds requester-consumed delivery metadata to subagent registry/delivery state.
- Adds a registry operation for marking descendant completions consumed by requester.
- Persists/restores the new delivery fields.
- Exposes the new runtime operation through the existing registry runtime shims.
Main files:
- `src/agents/subagent-registry-consumption.ts`
  - Implements durable requester-consumption credit.
  - Matches by requester session, explicit run IDs, and run-start window.
  - Records requester-consumption metadata and persists the updated run state.
- `src/agents/subagent-registry.types.ts`
  - Adds delivery/requester-consumption state fields.
- `src/agents/subagent-delivery-state.ts`
  - Persists and restores the new delivery fields.
- `src/agents/subagent-registry.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-registry-runtime.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-announce.registry.runtime.ts`
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-subagent-registry.runtime.ts`
  - Wires the new registry operation through runtime boundaries.
Requester-consumption paths:
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/subagent-followup.ts`
  - Reads completed descendant fallback replies and returns both formatted fallback text and the consumed descendant run IDs.
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-dispatch.ts`
  - Applies cron fallback consumption credit when cron adopts explicit descendant fallback output, before the final outbound send.
- `src/agents/subagent-announce.ts`
  - Credits nested/direct child completions when their output is included in the requester-consumed announcement/wake result.
  - Uses the same latest-child dedupe input for rendering and consumed-run credit so stale child rows are not credited.
- `src/agents/subagent-announce-output.ts`
  - Keeps latest-child dedupe reusable while preserving caller-specific fields such as `runId`.

## Tests / Verification

Coverage added or extended for:
- positive requester-consumed descendant credit;
- no credit for mismatched requester session;
- no credit outside the requester run-start window;
- no credit without explicit consumed run IDs;
- persisted/restored requester-consumption delivery fields;
- cron fallback credit only after successful outbound delivery;
- cleanup/finalize treating `delivery.status === "delivered"` as proof;
- nested/direct child announcement credit;
- stale-vs-current child dedupe, including a negative assertion that stale child run IDs are not credited when stale output is not rendered.
Primary test files:
- `src/agents/subagent-registry-consumption.test.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-delivery-state.test.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-registry-completion.test.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-registry.lifecycle-retry-grace.e2e.test.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-announce.format.e2e.test.ts`
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/subagent-followup.test.ts`
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-dispatch.double-announce.test.ts`

## Evidence

### Rebase/Squash/Proof

- Common upstream base: `13ecca5408cbc94e66105608bfe770d0fc660d76` (`origin/main`, `fix(telegram): back off session init spool retries`)
- Previous PR head: `604bc96e3bc716e545455c9ebaa81ef147a344f1`

- Rebased and squashed to one commit on the common base; pushed with `--force-with-lease`.
### Rebase/Squash/Proof

Current rebased/squashed PR head: `a6677b4d1ad6d58e4902bfb72d33be59b4b81d78`.

Latest pushed commit after same-base rebase and squash: `a6677b4d1ad6d58e4902bfb72d33be59b4b81d78`.

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs   src/agents/subagent-announce.format.e2e.test.ts   src/agents/subagent-registry-consumption.test.ts   src/agents/subagent-delivery-state.test.ts   src/cron/isolated-agent/subagent-followup.test.ts   src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-dispatch.double-announce.test.ts
```

Result:
- Type checks passed.

- Base: `31e941c3fc32a2bbb6aeb0a3ae6f5f46777b2a1b`

- Behavior proof refreshed: cron now credits `markDescendantCompletionConsumedByRequester` when it adopts explicit descendant fallback output, before final direct delivery, so a failed final outward send does not leave already-consumed descendant rows pending. SQLite persistence now derives `pending_final_delivery` only from active delivery statuses (`pending`, `in_progress`, `suspended`), so delivered/requester-consumed rows that retain payload metadata do not rehydrate as pending.
- Validation:
  - `git diff --check` -> passed.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-dispatch.double-announce.test.ts src/agents/subagent-registry.store.sqlite.test.ts src/agents/subagent-registry-consumption.test.ts src/cron/isolated-agent/subagent-followup.test.ts src/agents/subagent-delivery-state.test.ts` -> passed, 5 files / 124 tests across 3 shards.

## Compatibility and Risk

Risk is moderate because this touches subagent lifecycle/delivery finalization, but the implementation is deliberately constrained:
- no broad “assume delivered” fallback was added;
- no delivery status is credited without explicit consumed run IDs;
- matching is scoped to requester session and requester run-start timing;
- cron fallback credit is gated behind explicit adopted descendant fallback output;
- stale nested child rows are explicitly excluded after latest-child dedupe;
- persisted state changes are additive.
The main compatibility consideration is that existing delivery state can simply lack the new requester-consumption fields; restore logic treats those fields as optional.

## PR/Commit Surface Breakdown

Diff surface against `origin/main...HEAD` after the clean rebase:

target.title: fix(browser): pass control-client timeoutMs through guarded fetch dispatcher floors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Browser control HTTP client (`fetchHttpJson`) already resolved `timeoutMs` and aborted via `AbortController` + `setTimeout`, but `fetchWithSsrFGuard` did not receive `timeoutMs`. Guarded Undici dispatchers only apply connect/headers floors when `timeoutMs` is set; with signal alone, a hung control service can stall Agent browser tool turns (navigate/snapshot/act) until OS timeouts. Same family as Slack upload / Feishu / memory remote HTTP.

Open [#105102](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/105102) only improves malformed JSON error reporting; it does not add `timeoutMs`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Forward the already-resolved budget into the guarded fetch:

```ts

```

No new config/env surface. Existing AbortController timer and upstream signal composition stay in place.

## User Impact

**Before:** A browser control peer that accepted TCP without returning headers could stall Agent browser tool rounds beyond the intended client budget when only AbortSignal was wired into the guard.

**After:** Control fetches pass the resolved timeout (default 5s, or caller override) into Undici connect/headers floors as well as the AbortController timer.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(gateway): drain root work continuations before stop process exit
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105697

When a gateway process receives a direct stop signal (SIGTERM/SIGINT without a restart intent), any `session_end` plugin hooks already started by session reset/delete/compaction may be truncated before they complete. Affected plugins may lose database writes, memory summaries, or external resource cleanups.

#### Why This Change Was Made

Adds a bounded drain of the existing gateway root-work set to the direct-stop path. The drain uses a referenced `setTimeout` poll (not `.unref()`) so the timer keeps the event loop alive. Bounded at 2 seconds; the caller always invokes `exitProcess(0)` after return. Per ClawSweeper clarification: the force-exit watchdog is cleared at `run-loop.ts:705` before `handleStopAfterServerClose` is entered at line 710; the drain is self-bounded by its own referenced timer.

#### User Impact

Fixes an issue where WhatsApp inbound media downloads that stall after Baileys returns a stream (headers/start ok, then no further chunks) would block `downloadInboundMedia` forever via `saveMediaStream`'s unbounded `for await`, so inbound dispatch never produces an agent reply for that message.

target.title: fix(gmail): preserve bind errors across watcher output chunks
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the Gmail watcher enters an endless 5-second respawn loop when its gog serve process fails with an "address already in use" error under two independent conditions:

1. The error message is split across stderr pipe chunks (e.g. `"address alre"` + `"ady in use"`) and the per-chunk classifier misses the completed marker.
2. The final stderr fragment arrives after the child `exit` event but before `close`, so a restart decision made on `exit` never sees the completed marker.

A third edge case remains reachable even with chunk-carrying: when the combined stderr text exceeds the 512-byte retention window, `.slice(-512)` can discard a cross-boundary marker from the retained tail before classification runs.

## Why This Change Was Made

The stderr `data` handler now carries a bounded 512-byte tail across chunks and **classifies the untruncated combined text** before retaining only the last 512 bytes — so a marker completed across the old-tail/new-chunk boundary is detected even when the combined length exceeds the retention window. The restart decision moved from `exit` to `close`, so classification sees every fragment after stdio has drained before deciding whether to stop or to schedule a respawn. Bounded to the optional Gmail watcher serve path; no config or public API change.

## User Impact

Operators with an already-running Gmail watcher (or a stale port binding) no longer experience an infinite 5-second respawn loop when starting a second watcher. The watcher correctly stops restarts and logs a clear diagnostic.

## Evidence

**Before (RED) — exit-before-final-stderr (real child_process):** With stderr delivery paused so Node's documented `exit`-before-remaining-stdio ordering appears, deciding restart policy on `exit` misses the bind marker and would respawn:

```
BEFORE (decide on exit): addressInUse=false, wouldRespawn=true
events: ["exit:1:addressInUse=false"]
```

**Premise:** Node emits `exit` before all stdio is necessarily drained; `close` fires after streams close. `isAddressInUseError` matches `/address already in use|EADDRINUSE/i` against the untruncated combined stderr text so a cross-boundary marker is classified before the tail is truncated for bounded memory.

**After (GREEN) — same harness on `close`:**

```
AFTER (decide on close): addressInUse=true, wouldRespawn=false
events: [
  "exit:1:addressInUse=false",
  "data:\"listen EADDRINUSE: address alre\"",
  "data:\"ady in use 127.0.0.1:18788\\n\"",
  "close:1:addressInUse=true"
]
VERDICT: RED→GREEN
```

**After (GREEN) — real occupied-port production path:** Port `127.0.0.1:18788` held by a real `net.Server`; PATH fake `gog` that for `watch serve` calls `server.listen` and surfaces the OS error. Production `startGmailWatcher` → `spawnGogServe` ran once and stopped restarts (no second serve after 6.5 s):

```
[gmail-watcher] [gog] listen EADDRINUSE: address already in use 127.0.0.1:18788
[gmail-watcher] gog serve failed to bind (address already in use); stopping restarts. ...
SERVE_INVOCATIONS 1
```

**Negative controls:**
- Non-bind stderr split across chunks still schedules exactly one respawn.
- Complete bind marker still stops restarts.
- Exit-before-final-bind-fragment then `close` stops restarts (no respawn after 6 s).
- Cross-boundary marker with second chunk large enough to push combined beyond 512 bytes (824 bytes total):
  - Chunk 1: `"address alre"` → Chunk 2: `"ady in use "` + 800 bytes noise
  - truncate-before-classify would miss the marker; classify-before-truncate detects it → stops restarts.

**Focused tests:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/hooks/gmail-watcher.test.ts` — 13 passed (split-chunk, exit-before-final-stderr, exceeds-retention-window, and non-bind negative control).

**Diff stats:** net +4 prod LOC, +46 test LOC. `git diff --check` clean.

**Unverified:** Live upstream `gog` binary / Gmail API watch-start credentials on this host (fake `gog` on PATH exercised the real spawn + OS EADDRINUSE path instead).

*AI-assisted*

target.title: fix(ai): return default empty object schema when tool parameters is null
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `projectRuntimeToolInputSchema` receives null parameters (e.g., from `codex_app__automation_update` tool with no user automations configured), it was returning `schema: null` which causes strict providers like DeepSeek to reject the entire tool list with HTTP 400.

Error from DeepSeek:
```
Invalid schema for function 'codex_app__automation_update': schema must be a JSON Schema of 'type: "object"', got 'type: null'
```

## Why This Change Was Made

Null parameters semantically mean "no parameters" — not a schema error. The fix maps null to an empty object schema `{ type: "object", properties: {}, required: [], additionalProperties: false }` **without reporting violations**, so the tool passes through to the provider instead of being quarantined.

## User Impact

- **Before**: Null-schema tools (e.g., codex_app__automation_update with no automations) caused the **entire tool list** to be rejected with DeepSeek HTTP 400 or, after the previous partial fix, individual tools were silently quarantined.
- **After**: Null parameters produce a valid empty object schema at the projection layer with zero violations. The tool reaches the provider with a valid schema. No tool-list rejection, no quarantining.

## Evidence

### Core fix

The fix in `packages/ai/src/providers/tool-schema-json-projection.ts` returns a default empty object schema for non-object schemas, but only reports a violation for types that indicate a genuine schema problem (array, string, number, boolean) — not for null which semantically means "no parameters":

```typescript
if (!isJsonObject(projection.schema)) {
  if (projection.schema !== null) {
    violations.push(`${path} must be a JSON object schema`);
  }
  return {
    schema: { type: "object", properties: {}, required: [], additionalProperties: false },
    violations,
  };
}
```

### Provider-bound path trace

The exact path from null input to provider dispatch:

1. **`extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.ts:967`**:  
   `projectRuntimeToolInputSchema(descriptor.parameters, ...)` where `parameters` is `null`

2. **`packages/ai/src/providers/tool-schema-json-projection.ts:156`**:  
   null → empty object schema, zero violations

3. **`dynamic-tools.ts:971`**:  
   `projection.violations.length > 0` → `false` → tool NOT quarantined

4. **Provider dispatch**:  
   Tool reaches the provider with `inputSchema: { type: "object", properties: {} }` — accepted by DeepSeek, no HTTP 400.

### Integration test — full provider-bound path

```
── Step 1: projectRuntimeToolInputSchema(null, ...) ──
  Output schema: {"type":"object","properties":{},"required":[],"additionalProperties":false}
  Violations:    []    ← zero violations = tool passes through

── Step 2: 模拟 Codex dynamic-tools.ts 调用路径 (corrected behavior) ──
  Projected tools:    3 (message, codex_app__automation_update, get_weather)
  Quarantined tools:  0    ← null-schema tool is NOT quarantined
  Corrected schema: {"type":"object","properties":{},"required":[],"additionalProperties":false}
  Result: 所有工具正常发送到 Provider — DeepSeek HTTP 400 解决

── Step 3: Anthropic-family-tool-payload-compat 调用路径 ──
  Null schema result: valid schema — tool accepted by provider

── Step 4: 边缘用例验证 ──
  ✓ null       schema.type=object (0 violations)   ← passes through
  ✓ number     schema.type=object (1 violations)   ← genuine error, quarantined
  ✓ array      schema.type=object (1 violations)   ← genuine error, quarantined
  ✓ string     schema.type=object (1 violations)   ← genuine error, quarantined
```

### Unit tests

```
Test Files  1 passed (tool-schema-projection.test.ts)
     Tests  17 passed (17)

Test Files  1 passed (dynamic-tools.test.ts)
     Tests  100 passed (100)    ← all tool tests green
```

New regression test `"corrects null parameters to valid empty object schema"`:
- Verifies tool IS in `availableSpecs` (not quarantined)
- Verifies `quarantinedTools` is empty
- Verifies no quarantine warning logged
- Verifies no `tool.execution.blocked` diagnostic events
- Verifies tool call succeeds (`result.success === true`)
- Verifies execute handler was invoked

### Gateway server verification

```
Node v22.22.3 (SQLite 3.51.3) — started, healthz OK, ready OK
```

### Compatibility

- Null input → empty object schema, zero violations → tool passes through
- Array/string/number/boolean → empty object schema, violations reported → tool quarantined (genuine errors)
- Valid object schemas → unchanged

Fixes #106277.

## What Problem This Solves

Mattermost's default websocket factory set `maxPayload` but not `handshakeTimeout`. `createMattermostConnectOnce` waits for the `open` event; when a peer accepts TCP but never completes the websocket upgrade, that wait never ends. Slack relay and browser CDP already bound handshake waits at 30s.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Keep a private `buildMattermostWebSocketClientOptions` as the single production options surface (`handshakeTimeout: 30_000`).
- Default Mattermost `WebSocket` factory consumes that builder.
- Regressions observe that production wiring in source (knip-safe; no new unused exports) and prove stalled-handshake timeout returns control to `runWithReconnect`.

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** A Mattermost host that accepted TCP without completing the websocket handshake could pin the channel reconnect loop forever on that attempt.

**After:** Handshake waits fail closed after 30s (`WebSocketClosedBeforeOpenError` / close before open), allowing the reconnect loop to continue.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-websocket.ts`
- Production caller: `createMattermostConnectOnce` / `runWithReconnect` (same path as `monitor.ts`)
- Sibling: `extensions/slack/src/monitor/relay-source.ts` (`handshakeTimeout: 30_000`)
- Regression: `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-websocket.test.ts`
- ClawSweeper follow-ups addressed: production-wiring coverage + standalone timeout→reconnect output (including full 30s default-factory floor)

### Caller-path Vitest

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-websocket.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

```text
 ✓ ... > uses a 30s handshakeTimeout matching Slack relay 1ms
[mattermost handshake proof] timed_out=true name=WebSocketClosedBeforeOpenError message=websocket closed before open (code 1006)
 ✓ ... > fails connect when the websocket handshake never completes 203ms
[mattermost handshake reconnect proof] timeout_then_reconnect=true errors=WebSocketClosedBeforeOpenError,WebSocketClosedBeforeOpenError reconnect_delays_ms=50
 ✓ ... > returns control to reconnect after a stalled handshake 458ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  14 passed (14)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 8.05s
```

## Real behavior proof

**Commands run:**
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-websocket.test.ts --reporter=verbose
PROOF_MODE=short node /tmp/openclaw-mattermost-handshake-proof/standalone.mjs
PROOF_MODE=default-factory node /tmp/openclaw-mattermost-handshake-proof/standalone.mjs
```

**Before fix:**
Default Mattermost `WebSocket` options had no `handshakeTimeout`, so `createMattermostConnectOnce` could wait indefinitely for `open`.

**After fix:**
Production builder wires `handshakeTimeout: 30000` into the default factory. Against a TCP peer that accepts but never upgrades:

1. Short standalone run (200ms stand-in): timeout then reconnect attempt.
2. Default-factory floor (30_000 ms): first attempt fails at ~30s, reconnect schedules, second attempt also times out.

**Evidence after fix (Vitest):**
```text
[mattermost handshake proof] timed_out=true name=WebSocketClosedBeforeOpenError message=websocket closed before open (code 1006)
[mattermost handshake reconnect proof] timeout_then_reconnect=true errors=WebSocketClosedBeforeOpenError,WebSocketClosedBeforeOpenError reconnect_delays_ms=50
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  14 passed (14)
```

**Evidence after fix (standalone, non-Vitest):**

```text
[standalone] connect_attempt=1
[standalone] timeout_or_error name=WebSocketClosedBeforeOpenError message=websocket closed before open (code 1006) elapsed_ms=204
[standalone] shouldReconnect attempt=0 error=WebSocketClosedBeforeOpenError elapsed_ms=205
[standalone] reconnect_scheduled delay_ms=50
[standalone] connect_attempt=2
[standalone] RESULT timeout_then_reconnect=true connect_attempts=2 errors=WebSocketClosedBeforeOpenError,WebSocketClosedBeforeOpenError reconnect_delays_ms=50 elapsed_ms=457
```

**Evidence after fix (standalone default-factory 30s floor + reconnect):**
```text
[standalone] mode=default-factory hang_tcp_peer=ws://127.0.0.1:56911 handshakeTimeout_ms=30000
[standalone] connect_attempt=1

[standalone] RESULT timeout_then_reconnect=true connect_attempts=2 errors=WebSocketClosedBeforeOpenError,WebSocketClosedBeforeOpenError reconnect_delays_ms=50 elapsed_ms=60069
```

**What was not tested:**
Live Mattermost Cloud/server credentials; gateway process packaging beyond the production `ws` client options + reconnect policy used by `monitor.ts`.
